title: So Reddit has decided that plain HTML is unsafe
titleZh: 所以 Reddit 认为纯 HTML 是不安全的
author: montroser
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Reddit-The-Company If you don’t know Reddit, it basically is the host of many popular forums. And like any company which encourages you to “come for the cats [and] stay for the empathy,” Reddit seems to be in the business of extracting as much value as it can from said forums without completely destroying them. After all, simply fostering community is not a noble enough goal for the New Tech, and fortunately for Reddit, genuinely human-generated data is now gold in the LLM Age. You are welcome to read about the last time they decided to pluck the metaphorical liver from their communities. Reddit-The-Search-Results While I no longer wish to engage with Reddit, I still visit it occasionally, especially in the LLM Age. This is because appending site: reddit.com to a search query is basically a surefire way to find results written by genuine humans. Which, just to be extremely clear, I still find desirable. Now behind a login… sort of After doing such a query yesterday, to my absolute delight I was greeted with I guess this makes me old, but I use the original frontend for Reddit, old.reddit.com. I’m going to try really hard not to preach about why it’s a better frontend, but that’s all it is! A design for Reddit. Look, I know I’m a fringe user. I use Firefox. I noscript! I am no stranger to being forced off a product that worked just fine because someone decides to no longer support the two people who still use it.
It happened to my phone of 8 years, which works fine by the way, but is on too outdated of an OS. May it rest in peace in its tiny glory.
It happened to my tablet of 10 years, which works even better than my phone and holds a charge like champ, for the same reason.
It happened to the API for Stack Exchange used by my copy of their outdated app long removed from the app store. This one hurt me the most.1

comments.author: benjiro29
comments.textRawHtml:
As somebody who did plenty of scraping for his own little projects, lets just say that reddit their security concerns are just PR for "we do not want to keep supporting old.reddit".

While yes, you can not simply scrap new reddit as easily as a pure html scraper is cheaper to run. And while the new reddit its js "slow down" scraping as it need to run over a headless browser. Do you slow scraping down a lot?

No. Because you can simply spin up more instances and route over more proxies. Given the fact that you can scrap millions of pages per day, on a single cheap 1 CPU node...

The limiting factor for scraping a website is not html vs js / client vs headless browser. Its avoiding detection by running from different ips, faking browser information and masking your traffic to not give off the smell of automatization (and avoiding tls fingerprinting).

I wrote this type of stuff before we had AI to help write it, in a few days time. Now with a LLM at your fingertips in a few hours, you will have a complete working version with cloaking build in.

And the larger size difference does not matter, you can block irrelevant files via faked cache responds, to give the server the impression that your a repeat client, and no need to flood your browser instance with images, fonts etc. Some think that this is a defense, aka throttling you with increased bandwidth usage lol

So in my personal opinion, its not about dealing with scrapers, but trying to push people to new reddit, so they can finally phase out old reddit.

PS: So much fun reading new reddit on your phone browser, to have it pop-up a "use our app" banner, that prevents you from interacting with the website anymore. And even blocks firefox its scroll ability (and thus accessing to the browser its nav bar). Tip for people: delete the sites cookies and cache regularly, to prevent this usage tracking, so the banner newer shows.
comments.textZhHtml:
作为一个为自己的小项目做了大量抓取工作的人，我们只能说 reddit 他们的安全问题只是“我们不想继续支持 old.reddit”的公关。

虽然是的，但你不能简单地废弃新的 reddit，因为纯粹的 html 抓取工具运行起来更便宜。虽然新的 reddit 的 js 会“减慢”抓取速度，因为它需要在无头浏览器上运行。您是否会大幅降低抓取速度？

不会。因为您可以简单地启动更多实例并路由更多代理。鉴于您每天可以在一个廉价的 1 CPU 节点上抓取数百万个页面...

抓取网站的限制因素不是 html 与 js / 客户端与无头浏览器。它通过从不同的 ip 运行、伪造浏览器信息和屏蔽流量来避免检测，以免散发出自动化的味道（并避免 tls 指纹识别）。

在人工智能帮助编写此类内容之前，我花了几天的时间编写了此类内容。现在，只需几个小时即可获得法学硕士，您将拥有一个带有隐藏功能的完整工作版本。

更大的大小差异并不重要，您可以通过伪造的缓存响应来阻止不相关的文件，给服务器留下您是重复客户端的印象，并且不需要用图像、字体等淹没您的浏览器实例。有些人认为这是一种防御，又名通过增加带宽使用来限制您哈哈

所以在我个人看来，这不是为了对付抓取工具，而是试图将人们推向新的reddit，这样他们最终可以逐步淘汰旧的reddit。

PS：在手机浏览器上阅读新的reddit非常有趣，让它弹出一个“使用我们的应用程序”横幅，阻止你再与网站互动。甚至阻止 Firefox 的滚动能力（从而访问浏览器的导航栏）。给人们的提示：定期删除网站的 cookie 和缓存，以防止这种使用情况跟踪，以便显示较新的横幅。

children.author: wongarsu
children.textRawHtml:
New reddit is more annoying (to me as human, but also to scrapers) in two very important ways:

- old reddit shows more or less the raw comment tree, sorted, like HN. New reddit does aggressive folding. You get a couple comments for each branch and have to click "show more" to see more

- new reddit forces you to log in to view anything tagged NSFW, including entire subreddits. Old reddit does not enforce this, along with not enforcing some other restrictions reddit has introduced over time

Of course none of this stops a scraper. And there is still the API. But these things make it easier to detect scrapers because they have to make a lot more requests and have to handle user sessions that make them easier to track
children.textZhHtml:
新的 reddit 在两个非常重要的方面更烦人（对我来说，也是对抓取者来说）：

-旧的 reddit 或多或少地显示了原始评论树，排序，如 HN。新的 reddit 进行了激进的折叠。您会收到每个分支的几条评论，并且必须单击“显示更多”才能查看更多

- 新的 reddit 强制您登录才能查看标记为 NSFW 的任何内容，包括整个 subreddits。旧版 reddit 不强制执行此操作，并且不强制执行 reddit 随着时间的推移引入的一些其他限制

当然，这些都无法阻止抓取工具。而且仍然存在 API。但这些东西使得检测抓取工具变得更容易，因为它们必须发出更多请求，并且必须处理用户会话，从而更容易跟踪它们

children.author: tlonny
children.textRawHtml:
As I understand it, anything publicly viewable is free to be scraped without issue.

If you scrape stuff behind a sign-up, you potentially open yourself up to being sued for breach of ToS.

Now I'm sure the Chinese labs don't give a rats arse about that threat, but I imagine it stops the likes of Google, OAI, Anthropic from scraping and instead forces them to purchase the data.
children.textZhHtml:
据我了解，任何公开可见的内容都可以毫无问题地免费抓取。

如果您在注册后抓取内容，您可能会因违反服务条款而被起诉。

现在我确信中国实验室不会对这种威胁大意，但我想它会阻止 Google、OAI、Anthropic 等公司抓取内容，而是迫使他们购买数据。

children.author: benjiro29
children.textRawHtml:
Not how it works ... Anything public viewable is still subject to a TOS. And the whole copyright or whatever still applies.

If your argument was valid, we can scrape news websites and show their content freely. No ... You get sued and lose the case.

See Google News that got their behinds in court and lost. Short summaries are allowed / transformative, but you can not just take content (even without a login). Not without getting into civil court if somebody wants to press the matter.

Now, if you scrap and never make that data public or transform it (LLMs). Then it becomes a harder matter to deal with.
children.textZhHtml:
不是它是如何工作的......任何公开可见的内容仍然受 TOS 的约束。整个版权或其他内容仍然适用。

如果您的论点有效，我们可以抓取新闻网站并自由显示其内容。不...您会被起诉并败诉。

查看 Google 新闻在法庭上的失败。简短的摘要是允许的/具有变革性的，但你不能只获取内容（即使没有登录）。如果有人想追究此事，就必须进入民事法庭。

现在，如果你废弃并且从未公开或转换该数据（法学硕士）。那么事情就变得更难处理了。

children.author: avadodin
children.textRawHtml:
Old–school forums never left, still inhabited by the few boomers and genXers who could figure out the Internets back in the day and aren't dead yet.

The gamification of Reddit and the ephemeral nature of the main page along with subreddits with varying amounts of overlap contributed to more active interactions, though.

Some of the volume was lower quality but not all.

The boomer posts about his petunia breeding program on a BBS and he gets feedback half a year later after the other active user gathers the energy to travel to the computer room again.

On Reddit, maybe a zoomer would have asked if you can smoke petunias in Brazilian Portuguese, but that may still count as welcome human interaction to the old man.

None of that applies to new deaddit, though.
children.textZhHtml:
老派论坛从未消失，仍然居住着少数婴儿潮一代和一代人，他们能够在当时了解互联网，而且还没有消亡。

Reddit 的游戏化和主页的短暂性以及具有不同程度重叠的子 Reddits 促成了更活跃的互动。

部分内容质量较低，但并非全部。

婴儿潮一代在 BBS 上发布了他的矮牵牛繁殖计划，半年后，在另一个活跃用户积攒能量再次前往计算机房后，他得到了反馈。

在 Reddit 上，也许婴儿潮一代会用巴西葡萄牙语询问你是否可以抽矮牵牛，但这仍然可能算作与老人的受欢迎的人际互动。

不过，这些都不适用于新的 deaddit。
